mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand in the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when HOUST shows a sustained increase over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a single month signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when RSAFS grows by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a single month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates inflationary pressure in a high-rate environment, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points in the same quarter, it signals a strong economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% QoQ and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in Q
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 grows by more than 2% QoQ and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp in the same quarter.
